title: A Letters for the Summer
premise: Ansel Eastwick has spent ten years raising his daughter alone and running the last bookshop in the fading vineyard town of Marrow's Bend, hiding behind a counter and a carefully closed heart. Every summer since her death, an anonymous letter has arrived on his doorstep—tender, knowing, impossible—and he has kept every one, convinced they were a cruel kindness or a mistake. When Wren Calloway, the town's new winemaker, moves in next door, Ansel begins to recognize his own sentences coming back to him in her voice: she wrote the letters, having loved him from afar through a tragedy that also took something from her. As the vineyard's first harvest approaches, Ansel must choose between the safety of grief and the terrifying exposure of being truly seen, finally saying aloud the sentence he has rehearsed for a decade before the grapes come in.
about_author: Cyrus Nystrom is a former small-town bookseller who now writes love stories set in places where everyone knows your name and your history. He lives near a working vineyard and insists the best letters are the ones never sent—until they are.

chapters.title: The Tenth Letter
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. On the anniversary of his wife's death, the tenth unsigned summer letter arrives at the bookshop door. His daughter June catches him reading it and asks who writes them; he says he doesn't know. Beat: grief as routine, and the first crack of curiosity.

chapters.title: Moving Vans and Merlot
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Calloway arrives to revive the abandoned Harrow Vineyard next to the bookshop, all bravado over private doubts. She meets Ansel when June wanders into her rows of dead vines. Beat: guarded first impressions, an unexpected ease.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A slow day in the shop: shelving, regulars, June doing homework by the register. Ansel rereads the old letters and notices one mentions the vineyard. Beat: the past pressing closer than he'd like.

chapters.title: A Borrowed Ladder
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren borrows tools from Ansel and stays too long among the bookshelves, memorizing details she shouldn't know. A line from her letters nearly slips out loud. Beat: the thrill and terror of proximity.

chapters.title: What June Found
chapters.summary: June's POV (first time). Exploring the shop's back room, June discovers the box of ten letters and reads one meant for her father. Beat: a child's fierce protectiveness and dawning hope that her father might be happy again.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A late frost threatens Wren's budding vines; Ansel shows up at midnight with smudge pots and blankets without being asked. They work side by side until dawn. Beat: intimacy forged in shared labor, walls lowering.

chapters.title: The Letters I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback chapter: how Wren came to write the letters after a wrong she witnessed the night Ansel's wife died—a hit-and-run the town buried. Beat: guilt revealed to the reader, deepening stakes.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The town drafts both of them onto the festival committee; small-town scrutiny turns their friendship into gossip. Ansel pulls back, spooked. Beat: external pressure and self-sabotage.

chapters.title: Rain on the Reading Nook
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm strands Wren in the bookshop closing time; Ansel reads aloud to June while Wren listens unseen, hearing her own words echoed in his voice. Beat: longing sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel notices Wren knows things she shouldn't—the shop's broken step, his wife's favorite poem. Suspicion blooms alongside attraction. Beat: rising tension, trust wobbling.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Trellis
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel accuses Wren of prying into his life; wounded, she almost confesses but retreats instead. June witnesses the fight. Beat: midpoint rupture, both hearts bruised.

chapters.title: Silence Between Rows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks of cold politeness; Wren throws herself into the vines as harvest nears and considers leaving town before the truth can hurt anyone again. Beat: despair, temptation to stay invisible forever.

chapters.title: June's Campaign
chapters.summary: June's POV. June, armed with the letters' box, plays matchmaker badly—baking, excuses, a staged errand—that goes hilariously wrong. Beat: comic relief with an ache underneath; June decides to act herself.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Letter
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. An eleventh letter arrives out of season, postmarked locally, and this one names him. He realizes the writer is someone who loves him now, not just mourns him then. Beat: revelation ignites; he races to connect clues.

chapters.title: Handwriting
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Comparing the letters to a wine label Wren designed, Ansel matches the script. The truth lands like a physical blow—every tender word for ten years was hers. Beat: shock, vertigo, a terrible new question about why she hid it.

chapters.title: The Night It Happened
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wren finally tells Ansel everything: she saw the driver that night, reported it, was disbelieved and threatened into silence; the letters were penance and love entangled. Beat: full confession; justice outside the law becomes their shared burden.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Together they reopen the case quietly—old tire tracks, a retired deputy's conscience, a confession letter to the widow's family. Beat: purpose rekindling partnership; love and justice braided together.

chapters.title: Veraison
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The grapes begin to ripen; the driver, exposed, flees town and is arrested elsewhere. Wren waits for Ansel's verdict on her decade of deception. Beat: climax approaching; forgiveness still unspoken.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed for a Decade
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. On the eve of first harvest, Ansel stands among the vines and finally says it aloud: 'I have loved you since the first letter.' Wren answers with the words she never sent. Beat: emotional climax, the blurb's promise fulfilled.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: June's POV. The whole town turns out for the vineyard's first picking; June gives Wren the letter box, officially transferring custody of her father's heart. Beat: communal joy, family remade.

chapters.title: Letters for the Summer
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. One year later: a twelfth letter arrives signed at last, and Ansel writes one back. The bookshop window displays two chairs. Beat: tenderness, the loop closed.

chapters.title: Epilogue: What Grows Back
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Bottling day, the first vintage named 'Eleventh Summer'; Ansel and June press the cork with her. The final letter sits framed above the register. Beat: resolution—inheritance chosen, duty transformed into love.
